questions.q: What was the Doctor doing while the animals first went downstairs on the new ship?
choices: Leaning on the rail with a pipe, watching the islands fade
Steering the ship with the help of the tired swallows
Writing in his big notebook about the canaries and the sharks
Counting the bottles that were left in his medicine-bag
questions.evidence: the Doctor leant on the rail at the back of the ship with a pipe in his mouth

questions.q: What were the beds on the pirate ship made of, according to Dab-Dab?
choices: Old sail-cloth
Soft lamb's wool
Golden velvet
Primrose silk
questions.evidence: The beds downstairs are made of primrose silk

questions.q: Why did Jip think the pirates kept something special behind the locked door?
choices: He could smell gold and silver through the key-hole
He had seen a pirate carry a chest in there before
He guessed it was where the pirates kept their treasure
He heard coins jingling on the other side of the door
questions.evidence: Jip says it must be where the pirates kept their treasure

questions.q: What did the animals do after the Doctor found that the little door would not open?
choices: They called the swallows to pull the door open
They hunted all over the ship for the key
They tried to dig a hole under the door with their paws
They gave up and went to have their supper
questions.evidence: Then they all started to hunt for the key

questions.q: What did the walking-stick they found have inside it?
choices: A sword
A map
A flute
A key
questions.evidence: a walking-stick which had a sword inside it

questions.q: What was the first sound Too-Too said he heard behind the door?
choices: Some one turning the pages of a book
Some one walking up and down on tiptoe
Some one whispering a song to himself
Some one putting his hand in his pocket
questions.evidence: I hear the noise of some one putting his hand in his pocket

questions.q: How could Too-Too tell the person behind the door was unhappy?
choices: He heard the man sniffle and blow his nose
He heard the man calling out for his mother
He heard a tear fall on the man's sleeve
He heard the man kicking the door in anger
questions.evidence: the sound of a tear falling on his sleeve

questions.q: What does this chapter mostly show about Too-Too the owl?
choices: He knows the way across the wide sea better than the swallows
He can hear even the tiniest sounds that others cannot
He is the bravest of the animals when there is trouble
He can see in the dark better than any other creature
questions.evidence: Almost everything makes SOME noise--if your ears are only sharp enough to catch it
